content.text:
Yes, and you don't need to change any code. footprint isn't tied to Big Pickle:

- **Handover:** the plugin adds the handover to the system prompt (`opencode_plugin.js`, the `experimental.chat.system.transform` hook), so it works with whichever model OpenCode is using.
- **`footprint switch`:** it reads your default `model` from `opencode.json` (`switch.py:50`) and only falls back to Big Pickle if none is set.

So to use Ollama, add it as an OpenCode provider in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "ollama": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "Ollama (local)",
      "options": { "baseURL": "http://localhost:11434/v1" },
      "models": { "qwen3:8b": { "name": "Qwen3 8B" } }
    }
  },
  "model": "ollama/qwen3:8b"
}
```

Then run `ollama pull qwen3:8b`, open `opencode`, and pick the model with `/models`. With `"model"` set as above, `footprint switch` will also open the imported chat on Ollama.

Things to watch with local models (I haven't tested this end to end):
- **Tool calling:** use a model that supports it, like qwen3 or qwen2.5-coder. Without it, OpenCode can't edit files.
- **Context size:** OpenCode's system prompt plus the handover is long. If Ollama's context window is small, the start gets cut off and the model loses the handover. Raise `num_ctx` to 16k or more with a Modelfile or `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=16384 ollama serve`.
- **footprint's own model:** the local model in "Local model mode" also serves an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so it could be added as a provider the same way.

I can add an "Any model (Ollama)" section to the README with this config if you want.

Several free options work with OpenCode, so footprint's handover works with all of them. Free tiers and limits change often, so check the current limits before you rely on one.

**Hosted, free tier (no GPU needed):**
- **OpenCode Zen free models:** Big Pickle, which you already use. Zero setup.
- **Gemini CLI:** free with a Google account, with daily limits. Good at coding and has a very large context. It's a separate tool from OpenCode, but Gemini also works inside OpenCode with a free API key from Google AI Studio.
- **OpenRouter `:free` models:** one API key gives you many models, such as DeepSeek, Qwen-Coder and Llama. They're rate-limited. OpenCode supports OpenRouter as a provider.
- **Groq:** a free API key with very fast responses, mostly open models like Llama, Qwen and gpt-oss.
- **GitHub Copilot Free:** a monthly cap. OpenCode can log in with Copilot.

**Local, free forever (through Ollama):**
- **Qwen3-Coder / Qwen2.5-Coder:** the best open coding models; 7B–14B runs on a Mac with 16GB+ of memory.

- **DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite:** good if you're short on RAM.

**My pick:**
- **Day-to-day:** Big Pickle or a Gemini API key in OpenCode is closest to Claude quality for free.
- **Offline or private:** `qwen3-coder` on Ollama, using the config from my last message.
- **Backup:** OpenRouter's free models for when a rate limit hits.

```sh
brew upgrade ollama        # 0.13.5 is old; newer cloud models may need a newer version
ollama signin              # cloud models need an ollama.com account
ollama pull glm-5.3:cloud  # downloads only a small pointer; the model runs on Ollama's servers
ollama run glm-5.3:cloud "hi"   # quick test

Then add this to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, next to your existing `mcp` block:

"provider": {

```

Things to know:
- **Free tier limits:** Ollama's free plan has hourly and daily usage limits, and long agent sessions use them up fast. `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` is a backup when you hit the limit.
- **Context size:** the small default context window from local Ollama models doesn't apply here, because cloud models run with their full context on Ollama's servers.
- **footprint:** the handover and `footprint switch` work with this as-is, since `switch` reads the `"model"` line.

content.text:
Yes, there are two separate choices: the model, and the coding tool you run it in.

**Model, keeping OpenCode:** Big Pickle is just one model in OpenCode. You can switch to `ollama/glm-5.3:cloud`, a free Gemini API key, OpenRouter's free models, or Groq. footprint keeps working with any of them.

**Other free coding tools instead of OpenCode:**

| Tool | Free model | footprint support today |
|---|---|---|
| **Gemini CLI** (Google) | Gemini, free daily limit with a Google account | ❌ |
| **Qwen Code** | Qwen3-Coder, free daily limit | ❌ |
| **Codex CLI** (OpenAI) | needs an OpenAI key, or a local model through Ollama | ❌ |
| **Aider** | any model: Ollama, OpenRouter, Gemini | ❌ |
| **Cline / Roo / Kilo Code** (VS Code extensions) | any model, Ollama included | ❌ |
| **Goose** (Block) / **Crush** (Charm) | any model | ❌ |

footprint currently hands over context only between Claude Code and OpenCode. Getting it into the others is cheap, though, because most of them read a project instructions file at startup:
- Codex, Kilo, Goose and Cursor read `AGENTS.md`
- Gemini CLI reads `GEMINI.md`
- Aider reads whatever file you pass with `--read <file>`

So one small feature would cover most of them: a `footprint context write` command that saves the handover to `.footprint/HANDOVER.md` and points `AGENTS.md`/`GEMINI.md` at it.

**My pick:**
- **Stay in the terminal for free:** OpenCode with `glm-5.3:cloud` or Gemini as the model. footprint already works there and you change nothing.
- **Want it inside VS Code** (your wrapper idea): **Kilo Code** or **Cline**, both open source and able to use any model. They're closer to the editor setup you planned than another terminal tool.

Want me to build `footprint context write` so the handover reaches Gemini CLI, Codex, Aider and the VS Code extensions too?

content.text:
Mostly yes. Both tools are open source and free to install, but where the free model comes from differs:

| | Gemini CLI | OpenCode + Big Pickle |
|---|---|---|
| Tool itself | free, open source | free, open source |
| Free model | Gemini, by logging in with a personal Google account | Big Pickle through OpenCode Zen |
| Signup | Google account required | none |
| Limits | a daily request cap (about 1000/day at launch, now possibly lower); it often drops from Pro to the weaker Flash model when busy | rate limits; Zen's free models are promotional and may be pulled |
| Who can use it | personal Google accounts; company Google accounts may need a paid Code Assist licence; not every country | anyone |
| Your data | free tier may use prompts to improve Google's models (you can opt out in settings) | free Zen models may also log or train on your data |

**For "free for all users" of footprint:**
- OpenCode is the better default: no signup, works anywhere, and footprint already supports it.
- Gemini CLI is a strong second choice. It has a big context window and is good at code, but needs a Google login and has a daily cap.
- Neither guarantees free forever. If you need that, a local Ollama model is the only safe bet.

My numbers come from memory and could be out of date. I can look up Gemini CLI's current free limits if you want them exact.

content.text:
Yes. Users only need Node installed and run:

```sh
npm i -g footprint-trace
footprint context install
```

No git clone. The npm package `footprint-trace` holds everything, including the OpenCode plugin.

The catch: npm still has the old version.
- **Local:** `0.3.0`, with the OpenCode two-way handover and `footprint switch`.
- **On npm:** `0.2.0`, which users get today and which is missing those features.
- **Blocker:** `npm whoami` fails here, so this machine isn't logged in to npm. Last time, the publish was stuck on two-factor login.

Ways to get 0.3.0 out:
1. **Recovery codes:** if you saved them when you turned on two-factor, `npm login` accepts one in place of the code. Then run `npm publish`.
2. **Access token that skips two-factor:** on npmjs.com, go to Access Tokens, create a Granular token with write access to `footprint-trace` and "bypass 2FA" ticked. Then run `npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_auth[redacted] and `npm publish`. This needs you logged in on the website, which may also ask for two-factor.
3. **Publish from GitHub (my recommendation):** set up npm Trusted Publishing for the repo, and a small GitHub workflow publishes to npm whenever you push a version tag like `v0.3.0`. There are no tokens or one-time codes to manage after the one-time setup on npmjs.com.

If you're locked out of two-factor completely, npm support can reset it. That takes a few days.

content.text:
I checked what's already built.

**Already in place:**
- **Website:** Continue with GitHub works, `/account` generates and revokes keys, and only key hashes are stored, in a private `footprint-vault` repo in each user's GitHub. There is no database.
- **CLI:** `footprint login` (GitHub's device sign-in), `footprint key`, and `footprint sync push|pull`, which syncs through that vault repo.

**What doesn't work yet:** nothing actually checks the key. The CLI signs in through GitHub, not with the key, and nothing on the server accepts an `fp_…` key. So the "paste key, done" flow you described doesn't exist yet.

What each of the three features needs:

| Feature | Needs | Works with "no database"? |
|---|---|---|
| Account / key | The server must find the user from the key alone. Lazy fix: the key itself carries the user's GitHub login, encrypted with the server secret, so it needs no lookup. Revoking still works: the server checks whether the key's hash is still in the user's `keys.json`. | ✅ |
| Cloud context sync | Handover saved to the user's vault repo, and read back when a session starts on another machine. | ✅ (GitHub is the storage) |
| Model gateway | An OpenAI-compatible endpoint, `/api/v1/chat/completions`, that checks the key and forwards to GLM through Ollama cloud or OpenRouter. It must count requests per user, and serverless servers can't share a counter in memory. | ❌ needs a small store (Neon, or Upstash Redis) |

Before building the gateway, three problems:
1. **You pay for every model call.** Ollama cloud and OpenRouter free tiers are limited per account, so one shared server key gets throttled once many users share it. A free gateway for all users needs a paid upstream plan, or a per-user daily cap that keeps it small. Reselling another provider's free tier may also break their terms; check before launch.
2. **The GitHub login asks for too much.** It requests the `repo` scope, which is read and write access to *all* of a user's private repos. Businesses and enterprises will refuse that. Switch to a GitHub App that only gets access to the `footprint-vault` repo.
3. **Session data leaves the user's machine.** Fine for personal use, but enterprise customers will want a way to turn sync off.

**Proposed build order (smallest first):**
1. **Key → `footprint login fp_xxx`:** a stateless key, a `/api/me` check on the server, and the CLI saving the key. Nothing new to sign up for.
2. **Context sync with the key:** on by default, with an off switch.
3. **Model gateway:** Neon for per-user daily counts, plus one upstream model key you provide. `footprint login` also writes the `footprint` provider into `opencode.json`, so users configure no models.

Shall I start step 1? For step 3 I'll need to know which upstream model provider you'll pay for.

content.text:
Here's the walkthrough for a new user, once all three steps are built. Each step is tagged ✅ if it works today or 🔨 if it's still to build. The site's address isn't in the repo, so I've written "footprint website".

---

### Before you start
You need **Node.js 18+**, which gives you `npm` and `npx`, plus at least one coding tool:
- **OpenCode** (free): `npm i -g opencode-ai`
- **Claude Code**, if you already pay for Claude

---

### Step 1 — Create an account (1 minute)
1. Open the footprint website and click **Continue with GitHub**. ✅
2. GitHub asks permission; click **Authorize**. ✅
   - Behind the scenes, footprint creates a private repo `footprint-vault` in your GitHub. Your synced sessions live there, not with us.
   - 🔨 This permission prompt changes to "access to footprint-vault only" once the GitHub App switch is done.
3. You land on the **API keys** page. ✅

### Step 2 — Get your key
4. Type a label such as `macbook` and click **Generate API key**. ✅
5. Copy the key (`fp_…`). **It is shown only once.** If you lose it, generate a new one and revoke the old one. ✅

### Step 3 — Connect your machine (one command)
6. In your terminal, run:
   ```sh
   npx footprint-trace login fp_xxxxxxxx
   ```
   🔨 Accepting the key is new; today `login` only does GitHub's device sign-in.

   This one command:
   - saves your key to `~/.footprint/` (only you can read it)
   - installs the handover into Claude Code and OpenCode
   - adds a **footprint** model provider to OpenCode, so you configure no models 🔨
   - prints: `signed in as <you> · context sync on · model: footprint/glm-5.3`

### Step 4 — Start working
7. Go to any project and start your tool:
   ```sh
   cd my-project
   opencode
   ```
8. Start working normally. In your first session there's nothing to hand over yet.

### Step 5 — Come back later: footprint takes over
9. Next time you open OpenCode or Claude Code in that project, the new session already knows:
   - the goal, files touched and open todos
   - the last error, and where you stopped
   
   Want to switch tools mid-task? ✅
   - Moving from Claude to OpenCode or back: just open the other tool and it picks up from there.
   - Want the exact same chat in OpenCode? Run `npx footprint-trace switch`.

### Step 6 — Another laptop
10. On the second machine, run the same command with the same key (or a new one):
    ```sh
    npx footprint-trace login fp_xxxxxxxx
    ```
11. Open the project. The session continues from where you left off on the first laptop, because the handover syncs through your `footprint-vault` repo. 🔨

---

### Everyday commands
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npx footprint-trace context` | Preview what will be handed over ✅ |
| `npx footprint-trace status` | Who you're signed in as, today's model usage, and whether sync is on 🔨 |
| `npx footprint-trace sync off` | Keep everything on this machine (private or company code) 🔨 |
| Website → **Revoke** | Kill a lost key; every machine using it stops right away ✅ (the server-side check is 🔨) |

- A coding tool — any one:
  - **OpenCode** (free): `npm i -g opencode-ai`
  - **Claude Code**, if you already pay for Claude

---

## Step 1 — Create an account (1 minute)

1. Open the footprint website → click **Continue with GitHub**. ✅
2. GitHub asks permission → **Authorize**. ✅
   - footprint creates a private repo `footprint-vault` in your GitHub. Your synced sessions live there — not with us.
   - 🔨 Permission will shrink to "access to footprint-vault only" (GitHub App instead of OAuth `repo` scope).
3. You land on the **API keys** page. ✅

## Step 2 — Get your key

4. Type a label (e.g. `macbook`) → **Generate API key**. ✅
5. Copy the `fp_…` key. **Shown only once.** Lost it? Generate a new one, revoke the old. ✅

## Step 3 — Connect your machine (one command)

6. In your terminal:

   ```sh
   npx footprint-trace login fp_xxxxxxxx
   ```

   🔨 Key login is new — today `login` uses GitHub device sign-in.

   This one command:
   - saves your key in `~/.footprint/` (only you can read it)
   - installs the handover into Claude Code and OpenCode
   - adds a **footprint** model provider to OpenCode — no model setup needed 🔨
   - prints: `signed in as <you> · context sync on · model: footprint/glm-5.3`

## Step 4 — Start working

7. Open any project and start your tool:

   ```sh
   cd my-project
   opencode
   ```

8. Work normally. First session has nothing to hand over yet.

## Step 5 — Come back later: footprint takes over

9. Next time you open OpenCode or Claude Code in that project, the new session already knows:
   - goal, files touched, open todos
   - last error, and where you stopped

   Switching tools mid-task: ✅
   - Claude ↔ OpenCode: just open the other tool — it continues.
   - Want the exact same chat in OpenCode? `npx footprint-trace switch`

## Step 6 — Another laptop

10. On the second machine, same command, same key (or a new one):

    ```sh
    npx footprint-trace login fp_xxxxxxxx
    ```

11. Open the project → continues from where you left off on laptop 1 (handover synced through your `footprint-vault`). 🔨

---

## Everyday commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npx footprint-trace context` | Preview what will be handed over ✅ |
| `npx footprint-trace status` | Signed-in user, today's model usage, sync on/off 🔨 |
| `npx footprint-trace sync off` | Keep everything on this machine (private / company code) 🔨 |
| Website → **Revoke** | Kill a lost key; every machine using it stops 🔨 (server check) |

## If something goes wrong

- **"key invalid"** — revoked or mistyped. Generate a new one on the website.
- **"daily limit reached"** — free model cap hit. Resets tomorrow, or pick another model in OpenCode with `/models`.
- **No handover in a new session** — run `npx footprint-trace context`. Empty output = no recent session in that project yet.

"""footprint — learn a local SLM from your Claude Code transcripts.

Commands:
  setup                 create .venv + install the platform backend (mlx / torch)
  trace                 arm tracing: sessions from now on become training data (run before chatting)
  collect [project]     parse ~/.claude/projects transcripts -> data/{train,valid}.jsonl
  train                 LoRA fine-tune base model on collected data
  eval                  test loss + perplexity of the footprint adapter on held-out data
  serve                 OpenAI-compatible API at localhost:8399 (install runs this for you)
  install               auto-start server (launchd / systemd / Task Scheduler) + OpenCode /footprint
  context [install]     previous Claude session's state for this project; install = SessionStart hook
  switch [list|session] open latest (or chosen) Claude Code chat in OpenCode, full history; list = show ids
  status                what's collected/trained
  login                 GitHub device-flow sign in (personal environment)
  key new|list|revoke   manage API keys (hashes stored in your footprint-vault repo)
  sync push|pull        sync data/ + adapters/ across devices via your vault
"""
import os, sys

from . import config, context, service, switch, transcripts, vault
from .backends import get


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    cmd = argv[0] if argv else "status"
    if cmd == "train" and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(config.DATA, "train.jsonl")):
        sys.exit("no data. run: footprint collect")
    {"collect": lambda: transcripts.collect(argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else None),
     "trace": service.trace,
     "train": lambda: get().train(),
     "eval": lambda: get().evaluate(),
     "serve": lambda: get().serve(),
     "install": service.install,
     "context": lambda: context.show(argv[1:]),
     "switch": lambda: switch.switch(argv[1:]),
     "status": service.status,
     "setup": service.setup,
     "login": vault.login,
     "key": lambda: vault.keys_cmd(argv[1:]),
     "sync": lambda: vault.sync_cmd(argv[1:])}.get(cmd, lambda: sys.exit(__doc__))()

- **Node.js 18+** (gives you `npm` / `npx`)
- A coding tool — any one:
  - **OpenCode** (free): `npm i -g opencode-ai`
  - **Claude Code**, if you already pay for Claude

---

## Step 1 — Create an account (1 minute)

1. Open the footprint website → click **Continue with GitHub**. ✅
2. GitHub asks permission → **Authorize**. ✅
   - footprint creates a private repo `footprint-vault` in your GitHub. Your synced sessions live there — not with us.
   - 🔨 Permission will shrink to "access to footprint-vault only" (GitHub App instead of OAuth `repo` scope).
3. You land on the **API keys** page. ✅

## Step 2 — Get your key

4. Type a label (e.g. `macbook`) → **Generate API key**. ✅
5. Copy the `fp_…` key. **Shown only once.** Lost it? Generate a new one, revoke the old. ✅

## Step 3 — Connect your machine (one command)

6. In your terminal:

   ```sh
   npx footprint-trace login fp_xxxxxxxx
   ```

   🔨 Key login is new — today `login` uses GitHub device sign-in.

   This one command:
   - saves your key in `~/.footprint/` (only you can read it)
   - installs the handover into Claude Code and OpenCode
   - adds a **footprint** model provider to OpenCode — no model setup needed 🔨
   - prints: `signed in as <you> · context sync on · model: footprint/glm-5.3`

## Step 4 — Start working

7. Open any project and start your tool:

   ```sh
   cd my-project
   opencode
   ```

8. Work normally. First session has nothing to hand over yet.

## Step 5 — Come back later: footprint takes over

9. Next time you open OpenCode or Claude Code in that project, the new session already knows:
   - goal, files touched, open todos
   - last error, and where you stopped

   Switching tools mid-task: ✅
   - Claude ↔ OpenCode: just open the other tool — it continues.
   - Want the exact same chat in OpenCode? `npx footprint-trace switch`

## Step 6 — Another laptop

10. On the second machine, same command, same key (or a new one):

    ```sh
    npx footprint-trace login fp_xxxxxxxx
    ```

11. Open the project → continues from where you left off on laptop 1 (handover synced through your `footprint-vault`). 🔨

---

## Everyday commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npx footprint-trace context` | Preview what will be handed over ✅ |
| `npx footprint-trace status` | Signed-in user, today's model usage, sync on/off 🔨 |
| `npx footprint-trace sync off` | Keep everything on this machine (private / company code) 🔨 |
| Website → **Revoke** | Kill a lost key; every machine using it stops 🔨 (server check) |

## If something goes wrong

- **"key invalid"** — revoked or mistyped. Generate a new one on the website.
- **"daily limit reached"** — free model cap hit. Resets tomorrow, or pick another model in OpenCode with `/models`.
- **No handover in a new session** — run `npx footprint-trace context`. Empty output = no recent session in that project yet.

content.text:
I built step 1, key login. Rejected keys and connection errors are tested; a real key going through end to end isn't. That needs a GitHub sign-in in your browser. Nothing is committed yet.

**How it works:**
- The website's key now contains your GitHub login and token, encrypted with the server's secret (`fp_` + encrypted data). The server can tell who a key belongs to without a database.
- Revoking still works: the server only accepts a key whose hash is still in your `footprint-vault/keys.json`.
- `footprint login fp_xxx` checks the key with the server, saves it to `~/.footprint/key` (only you can read it), installs the handover for Claude Code and OpenCode, and prints `signed in as <you>`.

**Changes:**
- `UI-Web/lib/vault.ts`: added `verifyKey()`; `createKey()` now makes the encrypted keys.
- `UI-Web/app/api/me/route.ts` (new): send a key, get back `{login}` or a 401. It never returns the GitHub token.
- `footprint_core/vault.py` and `cli.py`: `login fp_…`; `footprint key new` now points to the website, since keys made on the command line can't be checked by the server. Removed the old key-generation code.

**Tested:** with no key, a junk key, and a correctly encrypted key that isn't in the vault, the server answers 401. The CLI gives a clear error for a rejected key, a missing `FOOTPRINT_API`, and an unreachable server. Type check and lint pass.

**Before shipping:**
1. **Test with a real key:** deploy, sign in on `/account`, generate a key, then run `FOOTPRINT_API=https://<your-site> footprint login fp_…`.
2. **Production domain:** I found none on Vercel, so the CLI needs `FOOTPRINT_API` set by hand. Tell me the domain and I'll make it the default, so users don't set anything.
3. **Old keys stop working:** keys generated before this change are rejected, so regenerate yours. Changing `SESSION_SECRET` also kills every key.
4. **Install with `npm i -g`, not `npx`:** with `npx`, the installed handover points into npx's cache, which can be wiped, and the handover would quietly stop. The guide should say `npm i -g footprint-trace` once 0.3.0 is on npm.

Next is step 2, syncing the handover to your vault using the key. Should I go ahead, or do you want to test step 1 first?

## Step 1 — Create an account (1 minute)

   - 🔨 Permission will shrink to "access to footprint-vault only" (GitHub App instead of OAuth `repo` scope).
3. You land on the **API keys** page. ✅

## Step 2 — Get your key

4. Type a label (e.g. `macbook`) → **Generate API key**. ✅
5. Copy the `fp_…` key. **Shown only once.** Lost it? Generate a new one, revoke the old. ✅

## Step 3 — Connect your machine (one command)

6. In your terminal:

   ```sh
   npx footprint-trace login fp_xxxxxxxx
   ```

   ✅ Key login built (needs `FOOTPRINT_API` until the site has a production domain).

   This one command:
   - saves your key in `~/.footprint/` (only you can read it)
   - installs the handover into Claude Code and OpenCode
   - adds a **footprint** model provider to OpenCode — no model setup needed 🔨
   - prints: `signed in as <you> · context sync on · model: footprint/glm-5.3`

## Step 4 — Start working

7. Open any project and start your tool:

   ```sh
   cd my-project
   opencode
   ```

8. Work normally. First session has nothing to hand over yet.

## Step 5 — Come back later: footprint takes over

9. Next time you open OpenCode or Claude Code in that project, the new session already knows:
   - goal, files touched, open todos
   - last error, and where you stopped

   Switching tools mid-task: ✅
   - Claude ↔ OpenCode: just open the other tool — it continues.
   - Want the exact same chat in OpenCode? `npx footprint-trace switch`

## Step 6 — Another laptop

10. On the second machine, same command, same key (or a new one):

    ```sh
    npx footprint-trace login fp_xxxxxxxx
    ```

11. Open the project → continues from where you left off on laptop 1 (handover synced through your `footprint-vault`). 🔨

---

## Everyday commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npx footprint-trace context` | Preview what will be handed over ✅ |
| `npx footprint-trace status` | Signed-in user, today's model usage, sync on/off 🔨 |
| `npx footprint-trace sync off` | Keep everything on this machine (private / company code) 🔨 |
| Website → **Revoke** | Kill a lost key; every machine using it stops 🔨 (server check) |

## If something goes wrong

- **"key invalid"** — revoked or mistyped. Generate a new one on the website.
- **"daily limit reached"** — free model cap hit. Resets tomorrow, or pick another model in OpenCode with `/models`.
- **No handover in a new session** — run `npx footprint-trace context`. Empty output = no recent session in that project yet.

#!/bin/sh
# footprint installer — no npm, no git. Needs python3.
#   curl -fsSL https://www.tracefootprint.space/install.sh | sh -s -- fp_yourkey
# Re-run any time to update. Keeps your data/, adapters/ and .venv/.
set -eu

APP="$HOME/.footprint/app"
BIN="$HOME/.local/bin"
SRC="https://github.com/Amanlabh/footprint/tarball/main"

command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  echo "footprint needs python3. macOS: xcode-select --install · Linux: install python3, then re-run."
  exit 1
}

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
echo "downloading footprint…"
curl -fsSL "$SRC" | tar -xz -C "$tmp" --strip-components=1

mkdir -p "$APP" "$BIN"
rm -rf "$APP/footprint_core" "$APP/skills" # fresh code; data/ adapters/ .venv/ untouched
cp -R "$tmp/footprint.py" "$tmp/footprint_core" "$tmp/skills" "$APP/"

cat >"$BIN/footprint" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
APP="$HOME/.footprint/app"
PY="$APP/.venv/bin/python"
case "${1:-}" in
  train|eval|serve|install)  # local model mode: one-time venv + backend
    [ -x "$PY" ] || python3 "$APP/footprint.py" setup || exit 1 ;;
esac
[ -x "$PY" ] || PY=python3
exec "$PY" "$APP/footprint.py" "${@:-status}"
EOF
chmod +x "$BIN/footprint"

case ":$PATH:" in
  *":$BIN:"*) ;;
  *)
    case "${SHELL:-}" in
      */zsh) rc="$HOME/.zshrc" ;;
      */bash) [ "$(uname)" = Darwin ] && rc="$HOME/.bash_profile" || rc="$HOME/.bashrc" ;;
      *) rc="$HOME/.profile" ;;
    esac
    grep -qs '.local/bin' "$rc" || echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >>"$rc"
    echo "added ~/.local/bin to PATH in $rc — open a new terminal to use 'footprint'"
    ;;
esac

if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
  "$BIN/footprint" login "$1"
else
  "$BIN/footprint" context install
  echo "installed. sign in: footprint login fp_yourkey (key from https://www.tracefootprint.space/account)"
fi

#!/bin/sh
# footprint installer — no npm, no git. Needs python3.
#   curl -fsSL https://www.tracefootprint.space/install.sh | sh -s -- fp_yourkey
# Re-run any time to update. Keeps your data/, adapters/ and .venv/.
set -eu

APP="$HOME/.footprint/app"
BIN="$HOME/.local/bin"
SRC="https://github.com/Amanlabh/footprint/tarball/main"

command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  echo "footprint needs python3. macOS: xcode-select --install · Linux: install python3, then re-run."
  exit 1
}

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
echo "downloading footprint…"
curl -fsSL "$SRC" | tar -xz -C "$tmp" --strip-components=1

mkdir -p "$APP" "$BIN"
rm -rf "$APP/footprint_core" "$APP/skills" # fresh code; data/ adapters/ .venv/ untouched
cp -R "$tmp/footprint.py" "$tmp/footprint_core" "$tmp/skills" "$APP/"

cat >"$BIN/footprint" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
APP="$HOME/.footprint/app"
PY="$APP/.venv/bin/python"
case "${1:-}" in
  train|eval|serve|install)  # local model mode: one-time venv + backend
    [ -x "$PY" ] || python3 "$APP/footprint.py" setup || exit 1 ;;
esac
[ -x "$PY" ] || PY=python3
[ $# -gt 0 ] || set -- status
exec "$PY" "$APP/footprint.py" "$@"
EOF
chmod +x "$BIN/footprint"

case ":$PATH:" in
  *":$BIN:"*) ;;
  *)
    case "${SHELL:-}" in
      */zsh) rc="$HOME/.zshrc" ;;
      */bash) [ "$(uname)" = Darwin ] && rc="$HOME/.bash_profile" || rc="$HOME/.bashrc" ;;
      *) rc="$HOME/.profile" ;;
    esac
    grep -qs '.local/bin' "$rc" || echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >>"$rc"
    echo "added ~/.local/bin to PATH in $rc — open a new terminal to use 'footprint'"
    ;;
esac

if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
  "$BIN/footprint" login "$1"
else
  "$BIN/footprint" context install
  echo "installed. sign in: footprint login fp_yourkey (key from https://www.tracefootprint.space/account)"
fi

content.text:
Yes, npm is out of the picture now. Users install and sign in with one command:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://www.tracefootprint.space/install.sh | sh -s -- fp_yourkey
```

I ran the live script from the website in an isolated test home folder: it downloads, installs, puts `footprint` on the user's command path, and a junk key gets a clean 401.

**What the installer does:**
- downloads the code from GitHub as a 131KB archive, so users need neither git nor npm, only `python3`
- installs into `~/.footprint/app` and adds a `footprint` command in `~/.local/bin`, plus a line in `.zshrc` or `.bashrc` so it's found
- signs in with the key and installs the Claude Code and OpenCode handover
- updates by re-running the same command; trained data and models are kept

**Website changes:** after **Generate API key**, the account page shows the full command with the key already filled in, ready to copy. It also shows `footprint login fp_…` for machines that already have footprint. The home and docs pages now show the curl command instead of npm. `newuserguide.md` is updated to match.

Pushed as `2ac2e83`, and Vercel deployed it.

**Gaps:**
- **Windows:** npm covered it, this script doesn't. Adding it is a small PowerShell version (`irm …/install.ps1 | iex`).
- **Every push to `main` ships to users immediately.** Once you have real users, point the installer at tagged releases instead.
- **The key stays in shell history:** it's part of the command users type. That's typical for install commands like this, and revoking a leaked key on the website kills it.

Your next test is the same as before: generate a real key on the website and paste the command it shows you. Then step 2, syncing the handover between machines.

# footprint — Known Gaps

Open issues in the website-key + curl-installer flow. Newest work: `2ac2e83` (2026-11-02).

## Install

| Gap | Impact | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **No Windows installer** | `install.sh` is macOS/Linux only; npm used to cover Windows | `install.ps1` (`irm https://www.tracefootprint.space/install.ps1 \| iex`) |
| **Installer ships `main` tip** | Every push to `main` reaches users on next install/update — a broken commit breaks everyone | Point installer at tagged GitHub releases |
| **Key in shell history** | `… \| sh -s -- fp_key` leaves the key in `~/.zsh_history` | Accept (revoke kills a leaked key) or prompt for the key instead of an argument |
| **Removed files linger on update** | Re-install overwrites `footprint_core/` + `skills/` only; deleted files elsewhere in `~/.footprint/app` stay | Fine for now; wipe all code paths except `data/ adapters/ .venv/` if it bites |
| **npm package stale** | npm has `0.2.0` (no key login); footer still links npm | Unpublish/deprecate or publish once more; remove footer link |
| **Needs python3** | Machines without Python can't install | macOS: `xcode-select --install`; or ship a single binary later |

## Keys & auth

| Gap | Impact | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Real-key end-to-end test pending** | Only the reject paths are verified on production | Sign in on `/account`, generate a key, run the shown command |
| **GitHub OAuth asks `repo` scope** | Read/write to *all* user's private repos — businesses/enterprises will refuse | GitHub App with access to `footprint-vault` only |
| **Old keys invalid** | Keys made before `050bd7f` are rejected | Regenerate on the website |
| **`SESSION_SECRET` rotation kills all keys** | Changing the secret logs every user out of every machine | Never rotate casually; support two secrets during a rotation if needed |
| **Key verify = 1 GitHub API call** | Fine for login; too slow / rate-limited for a model gateway | Cache verified keys (short TTL) when the gateway lands |
| **CLI `sync push\|pull` + `key list\|revoke` still use GitHub device flow** | Needs `FOOTPRINT_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, which is empty by default → broken for users | Move sync/keys to the server, authenticated by the `fp_` key (step 2) |

## Not built yet

| Gap | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Step 2 — cloud context sync** | Handover saved to the user's vault, read on another machine; `footprint sync off` for private/company code |
| **Step 3 — model gateway** | `/api/v1/chat/completions` with the key; `login` adds a `footprint` provider to `opencode.json` |
| **`footprint status` (account view)** | Signed-in user, today's usage, sync on/off |

## Model gateway — decide before building

| Gap | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Who pays** | Every model call costs; free upstream tiers (Ollama cloud, OpenRouter) are per-account limited, so one shared key gets throttled at scale |
| **Needs a store** | Per-user daily counts can't live in serverless memory → Neon or Upstash Redis |
| **Provider terms** | Reselling another provider's free tier may break their terms — check first |
| **Upstream choice** | GLM 5.3 via Ollama cloud, OpenRouter, Gemini, … — pick one |

## Enterprise

| Gap | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Session data leaves the machine with sync** | Needs opt-out (and probably default-off for orgs) |
| **No org/team accounts** | Keys and vaults are per GitHub user only |
